title: Edge transport mechanisms in small-ELM and type-I ELM regimes at JET using global gyrokinetic simulations
byline: Dicorato; Mattia; Garcia; Jeronimo; Görler; Tobias; De La Luna; Elena; Merlo; Gabriele; Fable; Emiliano; Jenko; Frank; Štancar; Žiga; Garzotti; Luca; Zotta; Vit
html:
Abstract:To explore tokamak operating regimes that combine high energy confinement with edge dynamics relevant for ITER, new regimes with small edge-localized modes (ELMs), referred to as baseline small-ELM (BSE), have been obtained at JET with the Be wall and W divertor. In this work, the edge transport mechanisms in a selected BSE discharge are compared with those in a standard H-mode with type-I ELMs using radially global gyrokinetic simulations with the GENE code. The simulations use experimental input profiles and include kinetic electrons and deuterium ions, electromagnetic (EM) effects, and the radially varying equilibrium $E\times B$ flow. At low toroidal mode number $n$, the type-I ELM pedestal is found to be unstable to kinetic-ballooning modes (KBMs), with radial mode structures covering the full pedestal. In the BSE regime, no KBM branch is found, and the same spectral range is dominated by hybrid ITG--TEM modes. The modifications of the linear modes by finite$-\beta$ effects are discussed in details. In nonlinear simulations of the type-I ELM regime, KBM-driven turbulence produces high transport levels that are resilient to the equilibrium $E\times B$ flow. By contrast, in the BSE regime, EM effects moderately increase transport, which is strongly regulated by the equilibrium $E\times B$ flow. The two regimes also differ in their radial turbulence organization and in the amplitude and persistence of the zonal shearing rate. These results identify the interplay between EM effects and equilibrium $E\times B$ flow as a key element of edge transport regulation.
